# Patchline Lab — Next Founders edition

A local measurement workbench for wearable-sensor research: map a recording, inspect exact evidence, compare a reference or repeat experiment, and reproduce the investigation from an exported workspace.

Live: [patchline-lab.vercel.app](https://patchline-lab.vercel.app) · [Public source](https://github.com/rishikrrontala-bot/patchline-lab)

Built by **Rishik Rontala**, solo. This separate edition preserves the original Patchline and its other hackathon entries.

## Run and verify

Node 22 or newer. No dependencies, account, API key or runtime AI service.

```sh
npm start
```

Open http://127.0.0.1:8789. Stop with Ctrl-C; optionally set `PATCHLINE_LAB_PORT`. Browser modules require HTTP. The preview serves an explicit public allowlist. Static hosting needs only the packaged public files.

```sh
npm test
node tools/verify-research.mjs
```

The first command runs independent domain/validation tests. The second executes 120 independent analytic engineering cases and verifies the 5,000-row external-recording pipeline, saving actual results and timings in `proof/research-verification.json`. Browser verification also exercises the complete workflow, print, finance, mobile layout and runtime privacy. See [verification](submission/VERIFICATION.md).

## Complete workflow

1. **Try a discrepancy investigation** loads a labelled changing synthetic control, modifies a copy gradually, and compares it with the unchanged control. Shape-only checks can pass while a supplied control reveals a discrepancy.
2. **Load recorded temperature** imports 5,000 credited environmental readings from UCI. Values remain unchanged, the classifier stays disabled, and 76 sampling gaps remain visible under the declared 60-second maximum.
3. Upload your CSV and confirm columns/units. One sensor is enough. Unselected channels are absent; blank values in a selected channel remain missing.
4. Load a reference/repeat recording, or use the original as a declared experimental control. Apply alignment, tolerance, uncertainty, coverage and reference-step assumptions.
5. Follow a finding to its exact sample and expand **Why was this flagged?** for values, neighbors and the rule.
6. Edit a named, versioned protocol; export it with the import profile. Applying a protocol resets controlled modifications so checks under the new assumptions remain explicit.
7. Export JSON, comparison, print or the complete workspace. Restore to recompute evidence. Restored measurements stay imported, and saved operation descriptions are unverified metadata.

## CSV and units

Comma delimiter, dot decimals and numeric elapsed timestamps; BOM, CRLF, quoted/escaped/multiline fields supported. Bounds: 1 MiB UTF-8, 5,000 data rows, 16 columns, 256 characters per field, minimum three samples. Duplicate/empty headers, ragged rows, malformed quotes, nonfinite numbers and reversed timestamps are rejected. Extra unmapped columns are allowed but omitted from normalized exports; retain the raw file separately.

Canonical example (select only channels present):

```csv
timestamp_s,temperature_c,wetness_pct,ph,glucose_au
0,32.4,40,6.0,34
1,32.5,41,6.1,35
2,32.4,40,6.0,34
```

Time: seconds/milliseconds. Temperature: C/F/K converted to °C. Wetness: percent/fraction converted to %. pH is dimensionless; glucose is arbitrary experimental AU. Suggestions need confirmation. Raw voltage is not automatically converted to a physical/chemical measurement.

## Comparison semantics

`current timestamp − offset` matches the nearest actual comparison timestamp within the declared distance. Reference samples are not reused. There is no interpolation or extrapolation. Surrounding reference reading changes above the declared step limit make evidence unavailable; this does not establish that the reference is defective.

For absolute difference `d`, uncertainty bound `u`, tolerance `t`: within when `d + u <= t`, exceeds when `d − u > t`, otherwise uncertain. Insufficient pairs/coverage produce an inconclusive result. Repeat differences describe change; reference discrepancies depend on the supplied reference. Neither proves sensor drift or calibration accuracy. Comparison readings are bounded to ±1 billion for finite statistics.

## Architecture

- `research-engine.js`: mapping, conversion, protocol validation, one-to-one comparison, explanations and strict workspace serialization.
- `economics-engine.js`: per-lab economics with labor, fees, acquisition/onboarding, replacement churn, first-month losses and hypothetical customer time value.
- `lab-engine.js`: full-recording checks, copied faults, internally owned traces, analysis-bound reports and the historical fault benchmark.
- `engine.js`: inherited synthetic generator/classifier. Imports/restores never regain internal ownership or a pattern score.
- `lab-app.js` / `workbench.js`: local interaction, replay, evidence navigation and exports.

See the [architecture walkthrough](submission/technical-walkthrough.html). QC and matching are linear in row count over a fixed channel set; display reduction preserves missing breaks while checks/exports retain every row. The 5,000-row bound is verified. Streaming, shared editing and enterprise load testing are not implemented.

The historical standalone synthetic benchmark remains separate: seed 42 gives 75 detected / 100 faulted, 25 smooth-drift misses and zero false holds / 100 clean. New reference tests do not retrospectively alter it. No real fault-detection accuracy is claimed.

## Independent dataset credit

[Room Occupancy Estimation](https://doi.org/10.24432/C5P605), Adarsh Pal Singh and Sachin Chaudhari, UCI, CC BY 4.0. First 5,000 S1_Temp values and original Date/Time are retained; timestamps alone become elapsed seconds without assuming a timezone. [Manifest](samples/uci-manifest.json) records sources, transformations and SHA-256 checksums. Reproduce with `python3 tools/prepare-uci-sample.py PATH_TO_PUBLIC_SOURCE_ZIP`.

Environmental temperature proves import interoperability, not smart-bandage, patient or calibration performance. No source endorsement is implied.

## Business, privacy and submission

The proposed $300 pilot and $99/month maintained-workflow service are hypotheses. The calculator exposes first-month losses and buyer-value shortfalls. No interviews, customers, commitments or measured savings are recorded. Read the [pilot](submission/PILOT-OFFER.md), [validation kit](submission/CUSTOMER-VALIDATION-KIT.md), [business model](submission/business-validation.md) and [Devpost draft](submission/DEVPOST-DRAFT.md).

Files stay in the current tab unless explicitly downloaded. No telemetry, accounts, hidden persistence or runtime network API exists. [LIMITATIONS.md](LIMITATIONS.md) and [MODEL_CARD.md](MODEL_CARD.md) describe the boundaries. No diagnosis, treatment recommendation or hardware control is provided.

GLM 5.2 through Featherless generated add-on modules and the earlier interface as a coding assistant, followed by local integration, substantial review corrections and independent tests. The delivered app never calls Featherless. Credentials, prompts, generation tooling and budget logs are excluded from the package; the authorized coding cap remains $10.

The silent five-minute demonstration and [voiceover script](submission/next-founders-pitch.md) support the entry. Rishik supplies narration and Public/Unlisted upload; submission is not claimed until confirmed.

## Buyer task-value worksheet

A separate worksheet starts with blank task, usage and setup inputs; only proposed fees are prefilled. Compare the same complete, correct reporting task. Enter estimates or self-reported measurements with a note; the app does not independently validate either. Negative time differences remain negative. Monthly labor value, full upfront fees/setup and payback are separate, with unavailable payback when net value is nonpositive. No avoided-error or clinical benefit is monetized. Export the actual applied inputs/calculations as JSON; edits invalidate the result. The browser workbench remains free to evaluate.

GLM 5.2 generated this pure module, DeepSeek V4 Pro reviewed the business specification, and independent tests caught accessor and exact-break-even boundaries before release. Current automated total: 112 passing tests. Browser tooling optionally uses Playwright plus installed Chrome; `npm install --no-save playwright` is needed only to reproduce browser checks.

## Finished demonstration

The release provides a 299.96-second silent MP4/WebM and a matched five-minute voiceover script. Seven chapter boundaries are 0, 30, 75, 140, 175, 215 and 250 seconds. `tools/finalize-demo.cjs` removes recorder holds and paces real captured actions; it requires full FFmpeg, `PATCHLINE_FFMPEG` if needed, and a hash-matching raw source/edit list. `--check` validates the edit without encoding. No app outputs or source measurements are generated or changed by editing. Voiceover and Public/Unlisted upload remain the builder’s final video step.

# Returnline

**Miss a day. Keep the thread.** A student returning after an absence can paste up to five class notices, review source-linked work and questions, and make a two-day catch-up plan based on time actually available.

Built by Rishik Rontala for ImpactHack 2026, October 1–7, 2026.

## What works

1. Paste class notices, or load a **clearly marked fictional example**.
2. Live analysis sends notices to Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite through one server route. It proposes tasks, dates, missing materials, and questions.
3. The server discards any proposed item whose quotation is not an exact substring of its notice. It parses only supported date phrases from that verified quote. The student can edit or remove every item.
4. Pure planning code places questions before blocked work, orders tasks by deadlines, flags unknown or conflicting dates, and calculates shortfalls against the next two days.
5. Print the brief or copy a question. Returnline does not message teachers.

The browser stores the active session in `localStorage`. There are no accounts or database.

## Run locally

Node 22 is required.

```bash
npm install
cp .env.example .env.local
# Add a Gemini API key to .env.local (never commit it).
npm run dev
```

`GEMINI_MODEL` defaults to `gemini-3.5-flash-lite`. The **Try the example** flow works without an API key and is labeled synthetic. It is not a substitute for the live AI path.

```bash
npm test
npm run typecheck
npm run build
```

## How source checking works

Gemini returns structured candidates, not a plan. Each candidate carries a `noticeId` and exact `quote`. A task’s date phrase must occur inside that quote. A blocker needs its own exact quotation. Candidates without verified evidence are omitted and reported. The planner then runs without AI.

Source checking establishes that the words occur in the pasted notice. It **cannot establish** that the AI interpreted those words correctly, that a teacher’s instruction is current, or that the student actually has the material. The review step and teacher questions are deliberate.

## Privacy

Live analysis sends pasted notice text to Google’s Gemini API. Avoid names, medical details, grades, and other private student information. The server does not persist notices; browser storage stays on the student’s device. Use the synthetic example for public screenshots and demo recordings.

See [LIMITATIONS.md](LIMITATIONS.md), [AI_USE.md](AI_USE.md), and [DESIGN.md](DESIGN.md).

# Set Room

A classroom SET competition built by Rishik Rontala. Each day, every class receives the same twelve cards with exactly six sets. Original is the default: find all six distinct sets on one fixed twelve-card board. Matched cards stay in place, shared cards can appear in multiple sets, and repeated triples do not count again. Refill rounds also finish after six sets and Sprint after three; those modes replace matched cards, guarantee another set, and allow repeated combinations when they reappear.

Live app: [Set Room](https://set-room.vercel.app).

## Use

Create a class league, enter class names one per line, and share its room code/link with the teacher’s other screens. Select the class and game version, then start. Classes can be changed directly from the class menu; switching during an active round asks for confirmation, ends that round, and preserves its progress in history. Each match is verified and saved by the server. The timer stops after the final valid set and the server saves the official time with the class and New York puzzle date. Found sets stay in a sticky sidebar beside the board on desktop, so the class can check previous combinations without scrolling. On mobile they follow the board. The leaderboard below the playing area shows each class’s best daily or all-time result and highlights the pizza leader.

Create an account or sign in with email and password, open your league, then choose Save room to keep it in your account. The shortcut remains saved after closing the tab or signing out. Open Saved rooms in the header to return on another device; sign out from the same dialog. Playing by room code does not require an account. Email ownership is not verified, and password recovery is not available.

The full round history includes completed, ended, and unfinished rounds; Load older rounds reaches every record, and CSV export includes all rounds. Practice provides hints and never saves ranked scores. Refill and Sprint offer Refresh cards, which deals a new solvable board without resetting the timer or found-set count. Those ranked rounds permit up to five manual refreshes; Original keeps cards in place after matches. Its Refresh board button above the table ends the active round and starts a new numbered puzzle with a fresh timer and six sets. Original standings keep each class’s fastest time across all puzzle numbers. Today resets at midnight in New York; All time and round history keep previous records. The room link includes the puzzle number so other screens receive the same board.

## Local development

Use Node.js 22.13 or later and install dependencies with `npm ci`. Create an ignored `.env.local` containing these configuration variables:

- `TURSO_DATABASE_URL`: a remote Turso/libSQL URL, or a local `file:` database URL for development only.
- `TURSO_AUTH_TOKEN`: the remote database credential; unnecessary for a local file database.
- `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`: a random secret of at least 32 characters.
- `BETTER_AUTH_URL`: the app origin, such as `http://localhost:3000` locally or the canonical live URL in production.

Run `npm run db:migrate` to apply the checked-in migrations. This command loads `.env.local` and creates both game and account tables. Start the app with `npm run dev`; a different port requires the matching auth origin. Build with `npm run build` and run that build with `npm start`. `npm run db:generate` generates migrations after schema changes. `node --experimental-strip-types --test lib/set.test.ts` checks the pure rules and generator.

## Vercel deployment

Vercel builds this directory as a conventional Next.js app using `vercel.json`. The Turso Cloud Marketplace integration provides `TURSO_DATABASE_URL` and `TURSO_AUTH_TOKEN`. Configure `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` and the production `BETTER_AUTH_URL` separately. Apply migrations against the intended database before serving requests; after pulling development configuration into `.env.local`, `npm run db:migrate` uses that database. Vercel requires a durable remote database and rejects a local `file:` database URL.

The original Sites/Vinext deployment used Cloudflare D1 and ChatGPT sign-in. Those are historical platform details; the current live app runs on Vercel with Turso and its own email/password accounts. Existing game records were migrated from the original database. Account bookmarks belong to the current app’s verified sessions, not to externally supplied identity headers.

## Architecture

Next.js 16 and React 19 provide the interface and route handlers. Pure deterministic SET logic lives in `lib/set.ts`; Turso/libSQL stores rooms, attempts, account sessions, and bookmarks. `lib/storage.ts` preserves the prepared-query interface used by the game routes. Better Auth handles email/password accounts through `/api/auth`, with the sign-in form at `/signin`.

Server timestamps are authoritative. Match claims validate the current board, advance atomically, and retry idempotently. `app/api/rooms/route.ts` scopes bookmarks to the live signed-in session. New attempts receive a private write token, so viewing their history cannot authorize a change. Room names and class labels render as text. Practice never writes an attempt.

See `LIMITATIONS.md` for supervision, timing, account, and privacy limits; `DESIGN.md` for the design system; and `VERIFICATION.md` for the distinction between historical checks and current deployment validation.

This is an independent recreation of SET and is not affiliated with its original publisher.

# Submitline

**Paste your hackathon rules and draft links. See what a judge can actually reach before you submit.**

**Live app:** https://submitline.vercel.app

**LovHack submission:** https://devpost.com/software/submitline (submitted October 4, 2026)

Submitline is a LovHack Season 3 entry built by **Rishik Rontala**. It pairs the official submission contract with unauthenticated link checks, GitHub public-visibility evidence, YouTube metadata, and deAPI Video Description observations. Each requirement stays **verified**, **blocked**, or **needs human review**; there is no readiness score.

## Run locally

Requires Node.js 22 or newer.

1. Run npm install.
2. Copy `example.env` to `.env.local`. Set `DEAPI_API_KEY` to enable video analysis and, optionally, `YOUTUBE_API_KEY` to check YouTube duration through the official Data API. Keep both keys server-side; never use a `NEXT_PUBLIC_` name.
3. Run npm run dev.
4. Open http://localhost:3000.

Without a deAPI key, link checks, requirement review, browser draft storage, and Markdown export still work. Video analysis reports its unavailable state explicitly.

## Deploy

Deploy as a **Node web service**, since link checks and video analysis use server routes. The included `render.yaml` configures Render's build, start command, and root health check. Keep `DEAPI_API_KEY` and `YOUTUBE_API_KEY` as server-side environment secrets if enabled. The same project can run on Vercel with its normal Next.js build; do not expose the key through a `NEXT_PUBLIC_` variable.

## Verify

- npm test — requirement extraction, status classification, address rejection, deAPI job states, and evidence labels.
- npm run typecheck
- npm run build
- npm run verify:ui — with the app running at http://127.0.0.1:3000 (or SUBMITLINE_URL), runs real Chrome desktop/phone checks and the example's broken live link, public GitHub repository, and public YouTube metadata path. Screenshots are saved in proof/.
- npm run verify:a11y — runs an axe-core WCAG audit at desktop and phone widths against both the empty workspace and populated evidence board. It excludes YouTube's cross-origin iframe internals, which the app cannot edit; the iframe has its own accessible title.

## How it works

The client keeps the draft and corrected requirements in browser storage. The /api/check route performs unauthenticated checks. It rejects local/private/credentialed URLs, resolves public DNS before each request, pins the vetted address for the connection, and revalidates every redirect. A GitHub repository is verified through GitHub's unauthenticated public API; other repository hosts remain human-review items. A reachable video page is never treated as proof of logged-out playback. With an optional `YOUTUBE_API_KEY`, Submitline reads duration through YouTube’s official Data API and blocks videos outside LovHack’s 2–3 minute window. When duration is unavailable, the entrant must confirm length manually; a YouTube oEmbed title is not duration evidence.

With the entrant's consent, /api/video/start sends a supported public URL to deAPI's Marlin_2B Video Description model. /api/video/job polls the documented pending, processing, done, and error states. The timeline shows model descriptions as visual observations, with YouTube jump links. deAPI reads pixels, not audio.

## Scope and source

LovHack's [requirements](https://lovhack-season-3.devpost.com/#challenge-requirements) require a project description, 2–3 minute video accessible without permission, technology list, and build-period disclosure. A working demo is requested whenever possible. A repository is an example of a prototype link, **not** a separate mandatory item. Pasted rules from another event are extracted conservatively and remain editable by the entrant.

This repository was created on **October 2, 2026**, inside LovHack's September 26–October 4 build period. The application code, design, and documentation are new work for this entry. npm packages are third-party dependencies; no earlier Rishik project code was copied. The built-in Northstar entry is explicitly fictional, and its public repo/video links are reference material for testing, not Submitline submission artifacts.

See [APP-BRIEF.md](APP-BRIEF.md), [WIN-CONTRACT.md](WIN-CONTRACT.md), [DESIGN.md](DESIGN.md), and [LIMITATIONS.md](LIMITATIONS.md) for the product contract, event research, visual direction, and honest boundaries.

## Product demo

Watch the [public product demo](https://youtu.be/kJ6F3ThVHcM), which YouTube Studio reports as 2:37, for real blocked-to-corrected link checks. The [local narrated, captioned master](proof/submitline-demo.mp4), [transcript](proof/DEMO-SCRIPT.md), [SRT captions](proof/submitline-demo.srt), and [thumbnail](proof/submitline-thumbnail.png) are included. The fictional example is clearly labeled; no deAPI output is shown without a real key.
